chunks: His existence weighed heavily upon his adversaries among the people, so they began inciting against him until he was denounced to the Abbasid Caliph [al-Qadir Billah Ahmad].

When [the Caliph] summoned him and questioned him about their denunciation and what they had charged him with, the Sheikh answered him in a manner that the Caliph accepted from him; so [the Caliph] elevated his standing, took revenge upon the informant, and humiliated him.

key_terms.السَّاعِي: the informant/slanderer — one who actively strives to harm another through false reports
key_terms.مَكَانَة: standing, rank, prestige — social and scholarly status in the community
key_terms.وِشَايَة: denunciation, tale-bearing — malicious reporting of someone to a ruler or authority

ai.seo_question: How did Sheikh al-Tusi respond when slandered before the Abbasid Caliph al-Qadir Billah?
ai.summary: This passage recounts the hostility faced by Shaykh al-Ṭā'ifa Muhammad ibn Ḥasan al-Ṭūsī from enemies who slandered him before the Abbasid Caliph al-Qādir Billāh Aḥmad (r. 991–1031 CE). The Sheikh's composed and satisfactory response to the Caliph led to his complete vindication and the public humiliation of the informant, demonstrating his unassailable scholarly and personal integrity.
